genZNote: Looks like C. diphtheriae under the microscope, tests negative on the toxin assay that actually matters.

habitat.hostAssociation: Normal commensal ('diphtheroid') flora of the skin and upper respiratory tract

microscopy.stain: Gram stain, Loeffler methylene blue for metachromatic granules
microscopy.appearance: Gram-positive pleomorphic rods with club-shaped ends

culture.growthCharacteristics: Facultative anaerobe, grows readily on routine media unlike some fastidious Corynebacterium species
culture.colonyMorphology: Small, white to grayish, dry colonies

identificationClues: Gram-positive pleomorphic rod in palisades/'Chinese letter' pattern, catalase positive
Non-toxigenic — Elek test negative, unlike Corynebacterium diphtheriae
Grows readily on blood agar and Loeffler's medium

diseases: Usually non-pathogenic; rare opportunistic infections (bacteremia, endocarditis, catheter-related infection) primarily in immunocompromised or line-associated patients
virulenceFactors: None equivalent to diphtheria toxin — non-toxigenic
clinicalImportance.transmission: Endogenous skin flora; opportunistic spread via breaks in skin or indwelling devices
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: Frequently isolated as a skin contaminant in blood cultures, complicating interpretation of true bacteremia versus contamination
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Distinguishing a diphtheroid contaminant from a clinically significant Corynebacterium isolate (and from toxigenic C. diphtheriae) relies on repeat cultures, clinical context, and the Elek toxigenicity test

examFacts.importantDisease: Rarely pathogenic — normal skin diphtheroid flora
examFacts.importantTest: Elek test to rule out toxin production and exclude C. diphtheriae
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: A non-toxigenic diphtheroid that mimics C. diphtheriae morphologically but lacks the diphtheria toxin gene
